value.body: State fisheries departments recruit graduates to run fish seed farms, support fish farmers and fishers, implement central and state schemes, and enforce fishing rules. Post names vary by state — for example Fisheries Development Officer, Fisheries Extension Officer, Inspector of Fisheries or Assistant Director of Fisheries.

items.label: Recruited by
items.value: State PSC or a state subordinate services board

items.label: Typical eligibility
items.value: B.F.Sc; some posts also accept a science master's such as M.Sc Zoology

items.label: Where you work
items.value: District fisheries offices, fish seed farms, harbours and reservoirs

items.label: Fish production in India
items.note: Up from ~95 lakh tonnes in 2013-14; India produces about 8% of the world's fish
items.source: Ministry of Fisheries, as reported (All India Radio)

items.label: B.F.Sc students enrolled
items.note: 5,010 across all years of the degree in 2023-24, about half of them women

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Apply when your state's PSC or recruitment board notifies fisheries posts. Selection is usually a written exam (general studies plus fisheries subjects) and, for some posts, an interview. Domicile and local-language rules often apply.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancies are notified irregularly and the number varies widely by state.
Coastal states and states with large reservoirs tend to have more fisheries posts.
Promotion leads to district and state-level fisheries administration.

value.title: Students enrolled in B.F.Sc
value.note: Total across all years of the course, not annual intake. B.F.Sc is the usual, but not the only, qualification accepted for these posts.
